circumstances: The controlled experiment from the previous day finished overnight. The researcher spends the morning inspecting the completed outputs and discovers a mixed result: the proposed method improves calibration on the standard in-distribution evaluation but the advantage largely disappears under distribution shift. This narrows the interpretation of the project rather than resolving it. The replication study is briefly revisited after an apparent preprocessing mismatch is found, but the exact reference preprocessing remains unclear. The afternoon shifts toward manuscript revision and figure preparation, with a shorter evening session used to document the revised hypothesis and open questions. There are several offline periods and a weekend interruption.

activities.title: Inspect the completed controlled experiment and investigate the shifted-evaluation result
activities.summary: The researcher inspected the completed controlled run, compared metric summaries, and checked recent literature to understand why the improvement seen on the standard evaluation weakened under distribution shift. The result suggests the method is more useful for in-distribution calibration than for robust calibration under shift, but the evidence is not yet sufficient to make a broad claim.

activities.summary: The researcher compared preprocessing code with the reference configuration and searched for reproduction details in public code. key_observations: The controlled experiment provides a clearer result than the earlier exploratory runs: the proposed method improves the standard in-distribution calibration result, but the improvement is much weaker under distribution shift.
The main research question should be narrowed or reframed toward when calibration improvements remain reliable under distribution shift rather than treating the method as uniformly better.
The replication discrepancy may involve preprocessing differences, but this is not established well enough to spend a large amount of time extending the replication yet.
The manuscript made substantive progress because the mixed result was incorporated into both the results and limitations rather than being treated as a clean success.
priority_alignment: The main research project remains the highest-priority thread and received the strongest analysis and writing effort.
The replication study was investigated but did not displace the main project's interpretation and manuscript work.
The manuscript is moving from exploratory notes toward a defensible results narrative.
important_uncertainty: It is still unclear whether the loss of calibration improvement under distribution shift reflects a real limitation of the method or a property of the current shift construction.
The replication mismatch may be caused by preprocessing differences, but the available evidence does not yet establish the exact reference pipeline.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Before launching many new variants, define one controlled distribution-shift comparison that tests whether the observed robustness gap persists, while separately recording the exact preprocessing assumptions needed to reproduce the reference result.

Do not treat the replication discrepancy as resolved merely because a preprocessing difference was found.
Do not rewrite the manuscript as if the method has failed completely; the in-distribution result remains informative.
